title: Burst reserve headcount orchestration — pricing sensitivity proforma
summary: Working proforma to model a 3-lane headcount plan (core / swing / surge) tied to a contracted burst-reserve product. Evaluates P&L sensitivity to: (a) per-token price +/- 15%, (b) utilization cliffs (65%, 85%), (c) contracted burst credits vs on-demand spend. Goal: recommend HC gating thresholds and a price floor that preserves 20% contribution margin under stressed demand.
assumptions: Average tokens per minute per request = 420 tokens (median workload)
GPU blend cost (amortized) = $1.35 / 1k tokens at 60% utilization; linear increase above 80%
Burst-reserve contract: monthly fixed credit pool 100M tokens for $80k with on-demand top-up at list rate
On-call / surge pool uses contractor GPU hours priced at 1.75x internal run-rate
Headcount fully loaded (salary + benefits + infra overhead): Eng $250k, SRE $200k, Product/Finance $170k
Goal contribution margin floor: 20% across hosted API product family
budget_rows: expected_token_demand (M) | 280 | 360 | 430 | 410 | 300 | median growth with seasonal Q4 spike
infrastructure_cost ($k) | 240 | 310 | 420 | 400 | 280 | includes cloud pass-through + spot premium
headcount_plan: lane: core | roles: infra eng (3 FTE), serving eng (4 FTE), SRE (2 FTE) | start: immediate | total_fte: 9 | fully_loaded_cost_ann = $2,250k
lane: swing | roles: throughput eng (2 FTE), infra support (1 FTE) | start: +2 quarters | total_fte: 3 | fully_loaded_cost_ann = $660k
lane: surge | roles: contractors (variable), on-call rotations | capacity: up to 6 contractor FTE-equivalents | cost_rate = 1.75x internal
phasing notes: hire 50% of core in Q3, remainder by Q1; swing hires conditional on sustained 12-week utilization > 70%
pricing_sensitivity: scenario: -15% price (avg $0.8075/1k) => revenue falls to $226k (Q3 base) and contribution margin drops ~5–7 ppts; under high demand quarters margin becomes negative unless contractor usage is capped
scenario: +10% price (avg $1.045/1k) => revenue rises to $293k (Q3 base) and margin improves +6–8 ppts; demand elasticity assumed small (inelastic) for enterprise customers
utilization cliff modeling: cost per 1k tokens rises 18% when GPU utilization > 85% due to spot failure and contractor substitution; effective margin exposure concentrated in Q4–Q1

breakeven price floor: to guarantee 20% contribution margin in worst-case (Q1 utilization spike + -15% price), required list price ~ $1.27/1k tokens or a mix of: (a) 10% surcharge on burst usage + (b) stricter contractor gating
scenario_analysis: Base-case (no price change): margins compress to single digits during Q4–Q1 due to seasonal demand and fixed contracted credits — runway okay but margin volatility high

Defensive-case (-15% price): immediate headcount hiring freeze for swing lane and re-evaluate core hire cadence; renegotiate burst contract to convert fixed credits to smaller monthly credits + lower unit rate for larger commit

Optimistic-case (+10% price): accelerate swing lane hires and authorize a small market dev budget to capture demand while preserving contribution margin; invest in additional caching and KV prefix optimization to reduce token consumption by ~3%

Operational mitigation: introduce a tiered surcharge for burst pool usage after crossing 120% of contracted credits; implement automated routing to cheaper regions when latency-tolerant requests detected
